## Promotion

`lr-c0.05-balanced` was registered as `churn` version 2 and took the `champion` alias.
Version 1 was the champion and now holds the `previous` alias. Its run recorded holdout PR-AUC 0.5364, Brier 0.1651; the incoming version scores holdout PR-AUC 0.5944, Brier 0.1962. Those outgoing numbers are read back from its own run rather than re-scored, which would have been a second look at the holdout.

## What the sweep showed

Every logistic regression beat every gradient boosting config on validation PR-AUC: the
worst linear model, `lr-c5.0-balanced` at 0.3999, is the only one that falls below the best
tree, `hgb-lr0.10-leaf15-l2` at 0.4623, and the top seven places are all linear. That is not
a statement about the two algorithms in general, it is a statement about this training set,
which contains no fibre-optic customer while 43.6 % of the holdout is one. A tree cannot
split on a one-hot column that is constant zero, and it flattens beyond the largest
`MonthlyCharges` it was trained on, so it scores the 461 fibre customers in the holdout as
if they were ordinary; the linear model extrapolates its coefficient and at least moves them
in the right direction.

The winner is worth reading twice. `lr-c0.05-balanced` takes the top spot on PR-AUC, and it
also has the worst calibration of the top five: Brier 0.1868 on val against 0.1604 for the
otherwise identical `lr-c0.05`, and 0.1962 on the holdout against a gate limit of 0.1981. It
passed by 0.0019. Selecting on PR-AUC alone rewards ranking and is indifferent to whether
the probabilities mean anything, and here it picked the reweighted model that ranks slightly
better and is calibrated noticeably worse. The gate caught it by two thousandths, which is
the argument for putting calibration into the selection rule rather than leaving it to the
last line of defence.
